text: comes back with this idol, and he tells the people: "Worship this idol."
And they obey him immediately. They start worshipping the idol.
And that is how [[shirk|شرك]] came back into the Arabian Peninsula.
There was no [[shirk|شرك]] in the Arabian Peninsula, and this is the man who brought it back: [[ʿAmr ibn Luḥay|عمرو بن لحي]].
So he orders the people to start worshipping this idol. They start worshipping the idol.
Over time, he brings more and more idols. He assigns one idol for each tribe. There are different tribes that are around, and he gives each tribe an idol.
So they start worshipping these idols at the [[Kaʿbah|كعبة]], at the House of Allah [[subḥānahu wa-taʿālā|سبحانه وتعالى]].
And like we mentioned, the [[Ḥajj|حج]] had been going on from the time of [[Ibrāhīm|إبراهيم]] [[ʿalayhis-salām|عليه السلام]]'s call.
Now, it was still going on during the time of [[ʿAmr ibn Luḥay|عمرو بن لحي]], but he changed the [[talbiyah|تلبية]].
You know the [[talbiyah|تلبية]], and we still say it today:

ar: لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ
translit: Labbayka Allāhumma labbayk, labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk, inna al-ḥamda wan-niʿmata laka wal-mulk, lā sharīka lak.

text: Now, he added a few words to this. At the end, he said:

ar: لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ، إِلَّا شَرِيكًا هُوَ لَكَ، تَمْلِكُهُ وَمَا مَلَكَ
translit: Lā sharīka laka illā sharīkan huwa lak, tamlikuhu wa-mā malak.

text: At the end, he said: "[[lā sharīka lak|لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ]]: O Allah, You have no partner except for the partners that You have, but You own those partners and You own what those partners own."
So he said, yes, Allah [[subḥānahu wa-taʿālā|سبحانه وتعالى]] is still the highest one, but He has certain partners, but He is the owner of what those partners own as well.
And he's talking about the idols here. So this is how he introduced [[shirk|شرك]]. Even into the call for [[Ḥajj|حج]], he introduced [[shirk|شرك]] into that as well.
And then he also said to the people: "If you are ever leaving [[Makkah|مكة]], if you ever have to go on a trip outside of [[Makkah|مكة]], you must take a stone with you from [[Makkah|مكة]]."

"You must take a stone with you from [[Makkah|مكة]], so that while you're outside of [[Makkah|مكة]], you worship that stone; you pray to that stone. And when you are in [[Makkah|مكة]], you worship the idols that we have here in [[Makkah|مكة]]."
"But when you're out of [[Makkah|مكة]], you must take a stone with you and worship those stones." So this is how [[shirk|شرك]] was introduced into the Arabian Peninsula.
They said, "Okay, look, everyone is going for [[Ḥajj|حج]]. Every year, people go and make this pilgrimage, so we will go for [[Ḥajj|حج]] as well."
"And when we're in [[Ḥajj|حج]], you know, there's so many people there, we can do whatever we want to do and nobody will know what's going on. We can do it without anyone finding out."
So after this, the people, they started to lose their sense of [[tawḥīd|توحيد]].
So they made that plan, and they met each other in [[Makkah|مكة]] at [[Ḥajj|حج]], at the [[Kaʿbah|كعبة]], at the House of Allah [[subḥānahu wa-taʿālā|سبحانه وتعالى]].
And they started worshipping these stones and calling upon idols besides Allah [[subḥānahu wa-taʿālā|سبحانه وتعالى]], and the society deteriorated.

And they did an act of immorality and indecency right there at the House of Allah [[subḥānahu wa-taʿālā|سبحانه وتعالى]]. They committed their [[fāḥishah|فاحشة]], they committed their immorality right there at the House of Allah [[subḥānahu wa-taʿālā|سبحانه وتعالى]].
And before, when [[Jurhum|جرهم]] was still in control of [[Makkah|مكة]], there was a situation that happened.
So to punish them, Allah [[subḥānahu wa-taʿālā|سبحانه وتعالى]] turned them into stones.
There were a man and woman from Yemen. The man's name was [[Isāf|إساف]], and the woman's name was [[Nāʾilah|نائلة]], and they were in love with each other in Yemen.
He turned [[Isāf|إساف]] and [[Nāʾilah|نائلة]] into stones. [[Isāf|إساف]] became a stone and [[Nāʾilah|نائلة]], she became a stone as well.
So [[Isāf|إساف]] went to the father of [[Nāʾilah|نائلة]] and proposed to her, asked for her hand in marriage, but the father of [[Nāʾilah|نائلة]] refused; he rejected him.

So the people, what they did—and this was before [[shirk|شرك]] came into the Arabian Peninsula, this is still during the time of when [[Jurhum|جرهم]] was in charge, before [[ʿAmr ibn Luḥay|عمرو بن لحي]].
So [[Isāf|إساف]] and [[Nāʾilah|نائلة]], they were very sad about this. They really wanted to get married. So they made a plan.

So what the people did with those stones, just so that people will have a reminder that this is what happens when you disobey and disrespect the House of Allah [[subḥānahu wa-taʿālā|سبحانه وتعالى]], this is what happens to you:
to serve as a reminder, they took the stone of [[Isāf|إساف]] and they put it on Mount [[Ṣafā|صفا]], and they took the stone of [[Nāʾilah|نائلة]] and they put it on [[Marwah|مروة]].

So the people would see these stones and they would remember what happened to these people and they would fear Allah [[subḥānahu wa-taʿālā|سبحانه وتعالى]]. They didn't worship those stones or anything.
But then when [[ʿAmr ibn Luḥay|عمرو بن لحي]] came and he introduced idol worship back into the Arabian Peninsula, what did he do? What do you think he did?
He took those stones—the stone on [[Ṣafā|صفا]] and the stone on [[Marwah|مروة]]—and he put them back in front of the [[Kaʿbah|كعبة]], and he told the people: "Worship these ones too."
So they started worshipping those stones as well. This is how [[shirk|شرك]] came into the Arabian Peninsula.
And it just gives you an idea of the society that the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, came into.
The reason I gave this whole introduction is so you know what kind of a society the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is being, you know, raised in.
Which type of society did Allah [[subḥānahu wa-taʿālā|سبحانه وتعالى]] choose to send His final and His greatest messenger? This is the society.
And this type of attitude of these people, it lasted all the way up to the time of the Prophet ﷺ.

And how do we know that? There's a [[ḥadīth|حديث]] of one of the companions, and he said that when they would leave [[Makkah|مكة]], if they would ever leave [[Makkah|مكة]], they would take the stone with them.
So it was still lasting up to the time right before the Prophet ﷺ. What [[ʿAmr ibn Luḥay|عمرو بن لحي]], what he introduced, it was still going on up to the time of the advent of the Prophet ﷺ.
So one of the [[ṣaḥābah|صحابة]], he mentioned that when we would leave [[Makkah|مكة]], we would make sure we take a stone with us.

And if we could not find any stone, we would take some dates from [[Makkah|مكة]], and we would make those dates into some kind of a statue or something, a figure, and we would worship those dates in place of stones instead.
So he mentioned, he said, like, "And you know, they realized it. After they became Muslims, they realized how ridiculous this was."

They said, "We would take those dates sometimes and make figurines or statues out of them, and when we were outside of [[Makkah|مكة]], we would worship that, we'd pray to it. But then we would get hungry, and we would find nothing else to eat, so we would eat our god!"
"We would eat what we were just worshipping!" Just to show the ridiculousness of this type of a belief.
This is the [[Jāhiliyyah|جاهلية]] society that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ came into.

And the reason why we gave this introduction is so you can see throughout the course, [[inshāʾAllāh|إن شاء الله]], how Allah [[subḥānahu wa-taʿālā|سبحانه وتعالى]], through the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, how He turned these people from the worst of people to the greatest generation of people that mankind has ever seen: the [[ṣaḥābah|صحابة]], [[māshāʾAllāh|ما شاء الله]].
How Allah [[subḥānahu wa-taʿālā|سبحانه وتعالى]] turned them around 180 degrees through His messenger Muhammad ﷺ.
And it's important to understand what kind of society it was so you can see the effect that the Prophet ﷺ had on that society.
And [[inshāʾAllāh|إن شاء الله]] we will talk about that, and we will continue to talk about the effects of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his birth next week, [[inshāʾAllāh|إن شاء الله]].

ar: وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ، وَصَلَّى اللَّهُ وَسَلَّمَ وَبَارَكَ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ
translit: Wa-Allāhu aʿlam, wa-ṣallallāhu wa-sallama wa-bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa-ʿalā ālihi wa-ṣaḥbihi ajmaʿīn.
